It is also narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih something similar to this. End of quotation.

﴿with a level place﴾, that is, a flat ground suitable for settling in, because of the amenities in it, ﴿and a spring﴾, that is, apparent water for a spring, and beneficial like the *maʿun* (a kind of water-source). It is a branch derived from two roots. Those kings and others who opposed him, despite their numbers and strength, were not able to kill him, neither in his childhood nor in his adulthood, as has passed in the quotation from the Injil (Gospel), which the Qur'an confirmed. This is despite his being a case of extreme weakness, being born from a female alone, with no helper but God. Nevertheless, God made his affair and the affair of those who followed him successful, and frustrated the disbelievers through him, and raised him to Himself in order to support this religion through him at the end of time, so that for the believers then there would be a success that no one before had attained. This was of the goodness and blessing of his Creator upon him.

**Mention of some of the proofs that he was a sign, from the Injil:**

John, one of the translators of the Injil, and most of the context is from Matthew, for I have combined the words of the four translators, said: "When the Feast of Tabernacles drew near, the brothers of Yasu' (that is, the twelve disciples) said to him: 'Depart from here and go to Yahudha, so that your disciples may see the works that are done, for no one does anything in secret while seeking to be known openly. Since you are doing these things, show yourself to the world.' Yasu' said to them: 'As for my time, it has not yet come, but your time is always ready. The world cannot hate you, but they hate me, because I testify against them that their works are evil. You go up to this feast; I am not going up now.'" Then he said: "When the middle of the days of the feast had come, Yasu' went up to the Temple and began to teach, and the Jews were marveling and saying: 'How does this man know the Book, when no one has taught him?' He said: 'My teaching is not mine, but is of the One who sent me. Whoever wishes to do His will will know whether my teaching is from God or from myself. Whoever speaks from himself seeks glory for himself, but whoever seeks the glory of the One who sent him is truthful, and there is no injustice in him. Did not Musa give you the Law, and yet none of you acts by the Law?'" Then he said: "On the great day, which is the last day of the feast, Yasu' stood calling out: 'Whoever believes in me, as the Scriptures have said, from his belly will flow rivers of living water.'" Many of the crowd heard his words and said: "This is truly a prophet." Others said: "This is the Messiah." Others said: "Does the Messiah come from Galilee? Has not the Scripture said that he is of the seed of Dawud, from Bethlehem, the village of Dawud, that the Messiah comes?" So fear arose among the crowds because of him.

Matthew said: "Then scribes and Pharisees came to Yasu' from Jerusalem, saying: 'Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders, for they do not wash their hands when they eat?'" Mark said: "Then the Pharisees gathered around him, and some who had come from Jerusalem, and they saw his disciples eating food without washing their hands, for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands, holding to the teaching of their elders; and what they buy from the markets, if they do not wash it, they do not eat. And many other things they hold to, such as washing cups, vessels, bronze objects, and beds." The scribes and Pharisees asked him: "Why do your disciples not walk according to what the elders have enjoined?" Matthew said: "He answered them and said: 'Why do you transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your traditions? Did not God say: Honor your father and your mother, and whoever speaks evil of his father or mother shall be put to death? But you say: whoever says to his father or his mother…'

'It is a gift (*qurban*) through which one benefits,' so he does not honor his father and mother. Thus you have nullified the word of God by your own tradition.'" Mark said: "And you do many things like this." End of quotation. "O hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you," and Mark said: "Yes, Isaiah prophesied of you, saying: 'This people draws near to Me with their lips and honors Me, but their heart is far from Me. They worship Me in vain, teaching as doctrines the precepts of men.'" He called the crowd and said to them: "Hear and understand. It is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth that defiles a person." Then his disciples came to him and said: "Know that the Pharisees, when they heard the word, were offended." He answered them and said: "Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted. Leave them, for they are blind leaders of the blind." Peter answered him and said: "Explain the parable to us!" He said: "Are you still without understanding? Do you not know that whatever enters the mouth passes into the belly and is expelled into the drain? But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart. This is what defiles a person, for out of the heart come evil thoughts: murder, adultery, fornication, theft, false witness, blasphemy. These are what defile a person, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person." Mark said: "Whatever is outside and enters the mouth of a person cannot defile him, for it does not reach the heart but goes to the belly and out. What comes out of a person is what defiles him, for from within come evil thoughts: fornication, murder, theft, [p. 154] greed, wickedness, deceit, lewdness, an evil eye, blasphemy, arrogance, folly. All these evils come from within and defile a person." End of quotation.

Among what is in it that is not permissible to take in its literal sense in our Law: the father, as has passed more than once.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 51:

When he (Allah) had made clear that Jesus, peace be upon him, followed the same way (minhaj) as his brother messengers in eating, in worship and in all conditions, He increased the confirmation of this by a clarification for those who had gone astray by believing in him what does not befit him. So He said, addressing all of them after destroying those among their people who had opposed them, in a manner that encompasses what came before, as a refutation of those who made this a reason to deny the message, and as a rebuke to those who innovated monasticism (rahbaniyyah) among the community of Jesus, peace be upon him, informing that every messenger was told the meaning of this speech and acted upon it, so that it was as if they had all been addressed with it at one time. He expressed it in the plural so that it would be more majestic for him and thus more likely to be accepted: ﴿O messengers﴾, from Jesus and others, ﴿eat﴾, you and those whom We saved along with you, after the destruction of the deniers.

When they rose above the rank of ordinary people, so that they were not earthly beings, He did not say ﴿of what is in the earth﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 168), and when they rose above the rank of the believers, He did not say "from the good things We have provided for you," so that they would be worshippers out of regard for the blessing or out of fear of retribution, as its explanation has passed in surah al-Baqarah. Rather He said: ﴿of the good things﴾, that is, the complete ones, which I have bestowed upon you by creating them for you, making them lawful, removing doubts about them, and making them desirable to the nature, beneficial to the body, and invigorating to the spirit. This is what is lawful and not repugnant, in accordance with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things and forbids them the vile things﴾ (Al-A'raf: 157).

He, glorified is He, indicated that what is lawful is an aid to obedience by His saying: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, that is, secretly and openly, without fearing anyone, for I have destroyed your enemy and made you inherit their land. Your deed is not restricted by gratitude or anything else, indicating that it is for His sake alone, for they are always in the station of witnessing (shuhud), in the presence of the One worshipped, and in independence from everything other than Him, even from independence itself. Then He urged them to sustain vigilance (muraqabah) by His saying: ﴿Indeed I, of what﴾, that is, of everything, ﴿you do, am All-Knowing﴾, that is, of perfect knowledge.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 52:

Since this was a justification (ta'lil) for the command that preceded it, the phrase ﴿And indeed﴾ is coordinated with its wording, with the particle read with a kasra in the recitation of the Kufan reciters, and with its meaning, since the word would deserve the fatha if the lam of causation (lam al-'illa) were made explicit, as in the recitation of the others. ﴿This﴾, that is, your call, O prophets mentioned above, both in summary and in detail, and your religion, which is united upon tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), or the community that I saved along with you from among the believers. ﴿Your community﴾, that is, your aim, which you should not direct your resolve away from, or the body of your followers, while they are ﴿one community﴾ with no dispersion at all. So long as they are unified, they are pleasing. ﴿And I am your Lord﴾, that is, the One who alone benefits you with creation and provision. Whoever affirms My oneness is saved, and whoever multiplies lords is destroyed.

(p-156) Since the address in this entire surah is to the sincere prophets and those believers who followed them, He said: ﴿So fear Me﴾, that is, place between yourselves and My wrath a protection by gathering My servants through calling them to My oneness without any division at all. This differs from surah al-Anbiya' (The Prophets), which begins with "mankind," since the unrestricted expression is more suitable for calling people to it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 53:

Since it is certainly known that the implied sense is: "The prophets feared God, who had sent them, and bore the heavy burden of what He had sent them with, so they called the servants to Him and desired to gather them upon it," he followed it with the particle of consequence (fa, "so") and the statement, expressed with the verb of cutting apart (taqattu'), because it conveys dispersion: ﴿So they broke up﴾, that is, the nations. He left out their mention only because their intention is clear, for the verse before it had explicitly stated that the prophets and those who were saved with them were one community with no disagreement among them. Thus it is known with certainty that the pronoun refers to the nations and those who came after them. For this reason, attention to the matter that had been one was more important, so he put first the words ﴿their affair﴾, that is, in the religion, after it had been united and connected ﴿among themselves﴾, and they became sects (shiya', sing. shi'a). This is the meaning of ﴿scriptures (zubur)﴾, that is, pieces, each piece being in the utmost strength, unity and firmness upon what it had come to of desire and misguidance, with every sect following a path of error away from the path of the nations and the straight destination. ﴿And each scripture (kitab) they wrote in their own desires, and they did not show mercy to themselves by what the guides called them to of unity and harmony, so they destroyed themselves with hatred and division.﴾ It is in the accusative because it is a second object of taqatta'a (to break up), as its derivation was explained previously in the discussion of the Prophets. It has become clear, as you see, very plainly, that this refers to those saved from the community of each prophet after the destruction of their enemies, meaning: this group whom I have saved with you is your community, being one community agreeing in the religion, with no disagreement among them; and just as your group is one, I am your Lord, there is no lord for you other than Me, so fear Me, and let none of you oppose My command, nor differ and separate, lest I punish the disobedient among you as I punished your enemies.

Since this is something no rational person would approve, it is answered as if one had said: "Did they accept that despite the clear exposure of its harm?" by His saying: ﴿Every faction (hizb)﴾, that is, every group, ﴿with what they have﴾, that is, of misguidance and guidance, ﴿are rejoicing (fariḥūn)﴾, that is, pleased, far from it being merely acceptance, without the misguided among them turning aside from what the messengers brought of guidance, nor heeding the lesson of what befell their nations because of their denial, of ruin.

Since this has yielded that misguidance, however clear, is not removed except by the Majestic One, He, glorified is He, consequently said, as consolation to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿So leave them﴾, i.e., leave them in their worst states, ﴿in their confusion﴾, i.e., the misguidance in which they have drowned, ﴿for a time﴾, i.e., until a term We have set for them before We created them, while We know everything that proceeds from them, and that it is a short term.

Since the cause of their delusion was their assumption that their state, in the expansion of provision in wealth and children, is the state of one who is promised (good), not one who is threatened, He denied this of them, as a warning to whoever has been preceded by happiness and for whom the best reward and more has been written. So He said: ﴿Do they reckon﴾, i.e., because of the weakness of their minds, ﴿that what﴾, i.e., those whom ﴿We extend﴾ in Our greatness ﴿with it﴾, i.e., We make it an extension for them, ﴿of wealth﴾ which We ease for them ﴿and children﴾ with whom We let them enjoy themselves.

Then he informed about "that" (anna), with evidence from al-Sulami's reading with the yā' (ya) below: ﴿We hasten for them﴾, i.e., by Our giving them abundance, with them as its object, in the speed of one who competes with another, ﴿in the good things﴾ which are not good things at all except that they are praiseworthy in their outcome. It is not so; rather, it is a calamity for them, because it is an enticement toward ruin, since they are not acting in what pleases the Most Merciful. ﴿Nay﴾, they hasten toward the means of evils, and the means does not come from anything except its causer. But they are like cattle ﴿who do not perceive﴾ that they are at the utmost distance from good things.

"We will draw them on step by step from where they do not know" (p-159).

When he had mentioned the people of division (ahl al-iftirāq), he followed them with the people of hypocrisy (ahl al-nifāq). It was as if it were said: "Who is it for whom the good things are?" So it was answered that it is the one who fears Allah. It was then said, expressing with what corresponds to the attributes at the beginning of the surah, beginning with fear (khashyah) because it is what drives the renewal of faith: ﴿Indeed, those who are﴾, that is, in their inner selves, ﴿in awe of their Lord﴾, that is, great fear of the One who is good to them and bestows favor upon them, ﴿fearful﴾, that is, constantly cautious.

Tafsir of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 23, verse 58:

﴿And those who believe in the signs of their Lord﴾, the heard and the seen, not those that come from other than Him, ﴿believe﴾. Their belief in them does not cease to renew itself, out of gratitude for His kindness to them.

Since a believer may sometimes be exposed to what has been mentioned before in his faith of association (shirk), whether overt or hidden, He said: ﴿And those who, with their Lord,﴾ meaning, the One whose bounty to them no one else bestows, alone, ﴿do not associate (anyone with Him)﴾ meaning, not any kind of association (shirk) at any time, just as no one shares with Him in His bounty toward them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 60:

When He had established for them sincere faith (iman), He removed from them self-admiration (ʿujb) by His saying: ﴿And those who give what they give﴾, meaning they give what they have given of acts of obedience (taʿat). Likewise is the reading of Yahya ibn al-Harith and others: "yaʾtuna ma ataw" (they do what they did), meaning they perform what they did of acts of righteousness (birr), so that the two readings agree in reporting of them the precedence (al-sabq) in good deeds. Then He mentioned their state, saying: ﴿And their hearts are fearful﴾, meaning intensely fearful, the fear having entered into their inner depths and roamed through every part of them, because they know that they cannot measure God with His true measure however hard they strive. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿that they are returning to their Lord﴾, meaning the One whose kindness toward them is abundant, ﴿returning﴾ through resurrection (baʿth), so that He will call them to account for the smallest and the least (al-naqir wa al-qitmir), and will recompense them for every little and much, and He is the All-Penetrating (al-Nafidh), the All-Seeing (al-Basir).

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The believer combines faith and fear (khashyah), while the hypocrite combines evil-doing and feeling secure (amn)."

Then he affirmed for them what implied that their opposites belong to their opposites. So he said: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., specifically, ﴿hasten toward the good things﴾, i.e., they race ahead in the manner of one who competes with another, ﴿in good deeds﴾. This implies the opposite of what was mentioned for their opposites in His words: ﴿and they are foremost in them﴾, i.e., toward them specifically, that is, toward their fruits. However, He expressed it with the particle "li" (lam) to indicate greater nearness to them and attaining them with safety, by making the good things a container (ẓarf) for the hastening, taking them in their literal sense for the transitive meaning (li-l-ta'diyah). ﴿Foremost﴾ over all people, because We Ourselves hasten to them with regard to the causes-of-effects (al-musabbabat) more greatly than their hastening in the means (al-asbab). It is also permissible for ﴿sabiqun﴾ to mean "those who are high-ranking" (ʿalin), from the valley of "My mercy precedes My wrath" (p-161), meaning that they are capable of them and are assisted in them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 62:

﴿And﴾ meaning, while the situation is that We do not burden them. But He generalized, so He said: ﴿We burden no soul﴾, meaning a disbelieving soul or a believing soul, ﴿except according to its capacity﴾. So no disobedient person can claim, "I was unable to obey," and no believer should think that We will hold him accountable for a slip or a lapse, for no one can measure Us according to our true measure, because the foundation of the created being is incapacity.

When deeds become numerous and their duration extends, their enumeration becomes difficult or impossible except through writing, so He (glorified be He) dealt with the servants in a manner they could understand, although He is free of need of that. So He said: ﴿And with Us﴾, meaning, in Our presence, in a manner that is the most wondrous of wonders, ﴿is a Book﴾. He expressed its being a means of knowledge by His saying: ﴿that speaks﴾ of what was written in it of the deeds of the servants, good and evil, small and great, ﴿with truth﴾, meaning the established reality that corresponds to what actually occurs. In it their deeds were written before their creation, with no addition and no deficiency. The guardian angels present to it each day what they wrote, of what they witnessed, with the verification of the decree for it, and they find it set down with its measures, its times and all its circumstances, so they increase in faith through it. And among its truthfulness is that none can deny any part of it.

When that implied the negation of injustice, he stated it explicitly, so He said: ﴿And they﴾, meaning the creation, all of them, ﴿will not be wronged﴾ by any wrongdoer, neither by addition nor by deficiency in deed or in recompense.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 63:

Since the implied sense is: "But they, with this, do not know," He said: ﴿Rather, their hearts﴾, i.e., the disbelievers among creation. It is also permissible that this turning away (al-idrab) is a substitute for His words ﴿Rather, they are not aware﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 56] ﴿are in confusion (ghamrah)﴾, i.e., ignorance that has drowned them, ﴿concerning this﴾, i.e., what We have informed them of from the Book that preserves (al-Kitab al-Hafiz), so they are disbelievers in it. ﴿And they have deeds﴾, and He affirmed the preposition to indicate that they have no deed that is absorbed in the lesser things, so He said: ﴿besides that﴾, i.e., beginning from the lowest degree of denial among the other sins, because of their denial of the Book, which necessitates their denial of the Resurrection (al-ba'th), which necessitates the absence of fear, which necessitates boldness in every grave matter. ﴿They are persistently doing them﴾, i.e., constantly, ﴿with nothing restraining them except their inability to do them.﴾

Since they were like cattle, fearing destruction only when they witnessed it, He set a limit to their deeds of wickedness by the seizing, saying: ﴿Until, when We seize﴾ — that is, with the greatness We possess — ﴿their affluent ones﴾, those who are the leaders and chiefs, ﴿with the punishment﴾. Then its breasts knelt upon them, and its rear and front parts came to rest upon them. ﴿Behold, they﴾ — all of them, the affluent ones and those who followed them by way of priority — ﴿cry out﴾, that is, they shout out in humiliation, abasement and anguish, without regard for pride, not out of arrogance. The root of *ja'r* (crying out, *ja'r*) is raising the voice in supplication, as al-Baghawi said.

Thus it is as if it were said: Will He accept their excuse, or have mercy on their humiliation? It is said: No. Rather, it will be said to them, by the tongue of the state or by the tongue of speech: ﴿Do not cry out today﴾ after those aspirations, for the man is one who does nothing in vain. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿Indeed, you from Us﴾, meaning specifically, ﴿will not be helped﴾, meaning in any way at all. And from Our not helping them, he finds no helper for himself, so there is no benefit in his wailing except the display of distress.

Then he gave the reason for their not being helped by His words: ﴿My verses were indeed recited to you﴾.

Since their greatness, by which they deserved to be attributed to Him, is sufficient to urge belief merely by hearing them, he framed the verb in the passive, His words ﴿are recited to you﴾, meaning: and they are the most manifest of things, from My friends, who are the guides and sincere advisers. ﴿So you used to﴾, meaning in a state that is like a natural disposition, ﴿turn back on your heels﴾ at their recitation, meaning you retreat backwards (yanka߯ūn), whether physically or figuratively, and one who walks in this manner does not look at what is behind him. Its present tense is, with kasra, yankiṣūn, and with damma, yankuṣūn; it was not read with the damma even as an anomalous reading, indicating that it is a retreat of arrogance and haughtiness, so it is at ease (bi-l-huwaynā). Had it been read with damma, it would indicate strength and thus convey aversion and flight. In al-Qamus (the dictionary) he said: nakaṣa ʿalā ʿaqibayhi yankiṣu wa-yankuṣu: he returned from what he had been upon of good; it is rarely used for evil; and ʿan al-amr nakṣan wa-nukūṣan wa-nikāṣan.

(p-164) Or, according to what you mentioned, it indicates a meaning whose implied sense is: "in a state of your being."

[Verse 23:67] ﴿Turning away from it, behaving arrogantly by it⦆ — i.e., by that turning back, with nothing other than arrogance, whether fleeing or otherwise, ﴿telling tales at night about it, speaking abusive words⦆ — that is, the obscene. Perhaps the reason He said ﴿sāmiran⦆ (telling tales at night) in the singular form is that each of them converses about the signs in company with others and alone with himself, a great deal of talk, like the talk of the night-companion, which is such that it never wearies; and He said ﴿tahjurūn⦆ — i.e., you turn away from them and say obscene things about them. He attributed it to the plural because some of them used to listen to it, though they did not utter obscenity about it. Or it is an expression of wonder that a group should gather upon such a thing, since a group is worthy that there should be found among it someone who perceives the truth and commands it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 68:

Since the verses, because of the miraculous eloquence and admirable wisdom they contain, call one to accept them after reflecting upon them, and since they would turn away from them and speak foully in describing them, at times calling them sorcery, at other times poetry, sometimes soothsaying, and at other times something else, this denial directed at them had a consequence. So He said, turning away from them to signal anger, and attributing the speech to the plural, which is more fitting for listening: ﴿Have they not then pondered over the Word?﴾ That is, the recited word addressed to them, by looking into its outcomes and consequences, even if they did not reach in their view the ultimate goal indicated by the idgham (assimilation), so that they would know that it necessitates coming near and joining, and describing with the best of speech. Perhaps He expressed it as "the word" to indicate that whoever does not accept it is not fit to understand anything of speech, but is rather among the ranks of the beasts. ﴿Or has there come to them﴾ in this word, of commands to monotheism brought by the Messenger, who is of the offspring of Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon them both, and what follows from those commands whose performance no rational person is ignorant of, and the prohibitions which—as the knower bears witness to the ugliness of committing them—the ignorant also decides upon; and [has there come to them] the message through a messenger from among mankind ﴿that had not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ those who were distant from Isma'il and before him.

When the complete man is the one who knows men through the truth, [the author] began with what he pointed to, then followed it with one who makes a thing known through familiarity with it, then with one who makes the truth known through men. So He said: ﴿Or did they not recognize their Messenger?﴾ That is, the one who came to them with this speech, for which there is no speech like it, and whose lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness they knew, along with the noble qualities that he possessed, to the point that they do not find in him, when realities are properly examined, any defect they could mention or any flaw they could imagine. This is what the authentic hadiths indicate, among them the hadith of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, may Allah be pleased with him, which is at the beginning of al-Bukhari (Sahih al-Bukhari), in the account of Heraclius, king of the Romans, questioning him about the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿So they are﴾, that is, as a consequence of their ignorance of him, ﴿to him﴾, i.e., to himself or to the speech he brought, ﴿deniers﴾. Thus they would be among those who rejected the truth because they were ignorant of the state of the one who brought it. So they attained (p-١٦٦) no share of either rank of people: neither the rank of the discerning scholars nor the rank of the ignorant imitators. In this is the utmost rebuke for them for their ignorance and their obstinacy, in that they know that he is the most truthful of creation and the highest in every noble quality, and yet they deny him.

Then, when he had finished with what might lead to attacking the speech or the speaker, he pointed to obstinacy regarding the speaker, the speech, and the Messenger, with His saying: ﴿Or do they say﴾, meaning: after reflecting on what he brought and not finding in it any aspect of attack, ﴿that there is in him﴾, meaning in their Messenger, ﴿madness (jinnah)﴾, meaning so he cannot be trusted, for he may confuse matters and bring something containing a flaw, even if the aspect of the flaw in it is hidden at the moment.

Since these possibilities are negated, especially the last one, which ordinarily entails confusion, and confusion entails falsehood, they know this noble Messenger better than anyone, that he was the most complete of them in creation, the most noble of them in lineage, the purest of them in character, the greatest of them in aspiration, the soundest of them in intellect, the most steadfast of them in opinion, the most pleasing of them in speech, and the most correct of them in deed, so He turned away from these and said: ﴿Rather﴾, meaning they did not recoil upon hearing the verses, nor did they become entertained (yasmuru) and abandon it (yahjuru) out of belief in anything from the past. Rather, they did that because this noble Messenger ﴿came to them with the truth﴾, which has no confusion in it in any way, and there is nothing more established or clearer than what is in it of tawhid and rulings. His challenging them with this Book clarified this, and they were unable (to meet it), so it is such that no fair-minded person could be ignorant of it. ﴿And most of them﴾, meaning while the state is that most of them ﴿are averse to the truth﴾, following ﻿(p-167) base desires and animalistic appetites out of obstinacy, while some of them abandon it out of ignorance and blind imitation, or out of fear that it will be said of them: "he has apostatized (sabi'a)." And some of them follow it by the grace (tawfiq) and support (ta'yid) of Allah.

When it was possible for someone to say, "What is wrong with him? Would it not have been better had he conformed to their desires, so that they would follow him, he would find rest, and they would find rest from these oppositions, which lead to quarrels and then to the greatest severance," He said, explaining the corruption of that: and perhaps this is a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*) from a subject who dislikes it, since its response is declarative, which justifies its being a *ḥāl*, as Shaykh Sa'd al-Din mentioned in the discussion of the *musnad* (predicate). Or it is coordinated with something whose implied sense is: "If they abandoned their aversion, they would love it; if they loved it, they would follow it; and if they followed it, they would become righteous and make others righteous." ﴿And if the Truth had followed their desires﴾, that is, in the fundamentals and the subsidiary matters, in states and in statements, ﴿their desires﴾, that is, their appetites which carry them away, being called desires (*ahwā'*) because of what the *iftiʿāl* (reflexive derived form, *ifti'āl*) indicates, ﴿the heavens would have been corrupted﴾ despite their elevation and firmness, ﴿and the earth﴾ despite its density and order, ﴿and whoever is in them﴾ despite their multitude, dispersal and strength, because of their claim of a plurality of gods. Had that been true, it would have led, by the proof of mutual prevention (*burhān al-tamānuʿ*), to corruption; and because of the divergence of their desires and their turbulence, which leads to conflict, as you see in the corruption that occurs when some aims are followed at certain times, until the Truth rectifies them by His wisdom and subdues them by His awe and His might. But We did not make the Truth follow their desires [p-168]. ﴿Rather, We have brought them﴾ by Our greatness ﴿their reminder﴾, which is the Book that is in the utmost wisdom. In it is the soundness of knowledge and the perfection of its order. When the ignorant one contemplates it, it restrains him from his ignorance, so he is made happy in his sayings and actions, and the good becomes clear to him in all his states. When the scholar reflects upon it, it elevates him to the summit of his perfection. Then the question arises about the One who sent it down, so necks submit; about the one upon whom it was sent down, so he is magnified in hearts; and about his people, so souls honor them, and heads are bowed in awe of them. Thus they have the greatest mention and the highest honor.

When they made what necessitates turning toward (the reminder) a cause of turning away, He said, marveling at them: ﴿So they are, from their reminder﴾, that is, which is their honor, ﴿turning away﴾. Their turning away does not cause Us to miss any purpose, nor does any harm reach Us by it; its harm returns only to them, and in every state it comes back upon them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 72:

When Allah, exalted is He, had refuted their charges against the one sent with the message and against the message itself, from the standpoint of their ignorance on one occasion and from the standpoint of their claim of its falsehood on another, He drew their attention to another aspect, of which they are the most knowledgeable of people regarding its falsehood, so that the claim to soundness would be established once the aspects of the accusations were negated. So He said, rebuking: ﴿Or do you ask them﴾, that is, for what you have brought them, ﴿for a payment (kharj)﴾. Al-Baghawi (p-169) said: a wage and a reward. Ibn Makturn said in al-Jam' bayna al-'Uba wa al-Muhkam: al-kharj and al-kharaj are something a people give out of their wealth each year in a known amount; and al-kharaj is the produce of a male or female slave. Al-Zajjaj said: al-kharaj is booty/revenue (al-fay'), and al-kharj is the tax and the poll-tax (al-jizyah). Al-Isbahani said: Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' was asked, and he said: al-kharaj is what is binding on you and it is obligatory for you to pay, while al-kharj is what you give voluntarily without obligation.

Since rebuking carries the meaning of negation, the placement of the particle of causation (fa') in His saying ﴿so the payment (fa-kharaj)﴾ is fitting, that is: do you ask them that, so that your asking would be a cause for their accusing you, and your not asking, because the payment of ﴿your Lord﴾, to whom you never directed yourself to anyone else and from whose door you were never absent at any time, ﴿is better﴾ than their payment. For His payment is neither cut off nor withheld from any of His servants, the wrongdoers, so how about the good-doers! It is as if He named it "payment" to indicate that He made the provision of every one binding upon Himself by a promise in which there is no failure. ﴿And He is the best of providers﴾, for He knows what makes every provided-for person right and what corrupts him, so He gives to him according to what He knows of him and does not make him need to ask.

Since the majesty of the King necessitates accepting what He brings and honoring it in any state whatsoever, He alerted that it is a truth whose acceptance confers honor even if it were not from the King; how much more so when it is from Him; how much more so when He is the King of kings and Owner of dominion; how much more so when the one who brings it is the elite of the servants and the most noble of creation, as the proof has established by negating all these slanders. So He said, conjoining it to "We gave them" (﴿آتيناهم﴾): ﴿And indeed you﴾, i.e., along with the negation of all these slanders, ﴿are calling them﴾, i.e., with this reminder, along with what we have already mentioned of the aspects that summon to following you, with the negation of all the slanders against you and against what you have brought, ﴿to a straight path﴾, in which there is no crookedness and no criticism at all, as sound intellects bear witness; so whoever travels it is brought by it to the goal and attains every honor. And the state is that they (are deviating from the path), but he expressed it with the attribute that drives them to blindness, so he said:

Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter ﴿do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ — therefore they do not fear retribution for it, ﴿deviate from the path﴾, that is, the one path beyond which there is no other path, because there is no means of reaching the goal except it. ﴿Are swerving﴾, that is, they are turning aside, withdrawing, inclining and deviating in all their states, proceeding by no method at all, but rather in blind groping (khabṭa ʿashwāʾ), because it is permissible that what is meant is the absolute "path" and that what is meant is the indefinite noun qualified by straightness.

When they were described as inclining (to deviation), and someone might have said that their earlier-mentioned supplication (*ju'ar*) was a way of following the path, He made clear that it should not be counted on, because it was incidental. So He said: ﴿And if We had mercy upon them﴾, meaning We dealt with them as one who is shown mercy by removing his harm. This is the meaning of ﴿and removed﴾, meaning by what We have of majesty, ﴿what harm is upon them﴾, which is what caused their supplication. ﴿They would persist﴾, meaning they would persist greatly (p-171) ﴿in their transgression﴾ that they were in before the supplication, which is their excess in opposing the truth and uprightness, ﴿wandering blindly﴾, meaning they would act with bewilderment and hesitation, like one who has no insight, on a course that deviates from the aim and strays from uprightness. Ibn Kathir said: this falls under the category of His knowledge of what would not happen, if it were to happen, how it would happen. al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: everything in which there is "law" (*law*) is something that will never happen.

Then he followed this proof with further confirmation, something that indicates that they would not walk the path except under compulsion, so he said: ﴿And We had already seized them﴾, that is, with what We possess of greatness, ﴿with punishment﴾, that is, with punishment in its general sense, such as the manifestation of the party of God over them at Badr and other battles. ﴿Yet they did not humble themselves﴾, that is, they did not submit with a submission that was like an innate disposition for them, ﴿to their Lord﴾, the One who is good to them after the trial. Its reality is that they did not seek to be His so as to honor the station of servanthood through abasement, submission, and compliance with His commands, leaving aside the desires of their own souls. The summary is that when He struck them with punishment, it was their duty to be His and not His partners', yet they neither acted in accordance with that requirement, by bringing it about, nor sought it. ﴿Nor did they supplicate﴾, that is, they do not renew supplication with submission, abasement, and humility at every time in a way that would become their habit. Rather, they remain upon what they were created with of arrogance and insolence, except when the two circles of the belly meet (i.e., when death comes), and no kind of (p-172) choice remains for them. The evidence for this is what the particle of limit (ḥarf al-ghāya, "until/even when") indicates, namely that the implied meaning is: "Rather, they persisted in their insolence."

Until, when We open against them a gate of severe punishment, by what We possess of majesty. This indicates that it is an opening of punishment, so He said: **upon them a gate**, one of the gates through which We overpower whom We will, such that its affair overwhelms them and they cannot repel it. **Of severe punishment** means the killing and capture on the Day of Badr, as said by Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father. Or it means the famine that He sent upon them in answer to the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ) in his saying: "O Allah, help me against them with seven years like the seven years of Joseph."

**Then behold, they are in it**, that is, in that gate, plunged in, unable to find any kind of escape from it, **in despair**, that is, bewildered, silent, hopeless about what is within themselves, unable to utter a single word. They have entered into *iblās* (despair, utter hopelessness), which is the absence of good, and they are deserving of dwelling in *Bawlas*, which is the prison of Hell. This is because they did not make humility a constant and inseparable attribute of theirs rather than an incidental one, nor fear of Allah a perpetual emblem that never departs from them, in recollection of His power and in magnifying His greatness.

Then he turned to address them, coaxing them with reproach, for when their punishment is mentioned, they are more likely to return. So He said: ﴿And He﴾, that is, they did not humble themselves before their Lord, while the reality is that He is the One and none other, ﴿who brought into being for you﴾, O you who deny the Hereafter, ﴿hearing and sight﴾, without any prior pattern. Perhaps He combined them (in the plural) because the variation in sight is greater than the variation in hearing. ﴿And hearts﴾, which are the seats of the intellects, so that by them you are higher than the rest of the animals. It is the plural of fu'ad (heart), which is the qalb (heart) because of its ignition (tawaqqud) and burning (taharruq), from al-tafa''ud, which is the burning. He used it here because the context is one of admonition and taking heed. Its plural is the plural of paucity (jam' al-qilla), indicating the rarity of those who possess this quality. Perhaps He also used the plural of sight (abṣār) in the same way, because it can also refer to insight (baṣīrah).

When He had depicted these blessings for them, blessings of which no heedless person doubts that there is no equal, and that if it were imagined that a human being could be given any part of them, he would not be able to repay the one who gave them, it became fitting to rebuke them for their ingratitude toward the Benefactor who bestowed them. So He said: ﴿Little is it that you give thanks﴾, to the One who bestowed these blessings for which there is no equal, and which no one other than Him can grant any part of, despite your claim that you are the most grateful of people to one who confers upon you even the least of blessings, of the kind that every person is able to provide the like of. Thereby you are lower than the dumb animals: deaf, mute, and blind.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 79:

When He had reminded them of these blessings, which indicate their creation, He stated it explicitly in His words: ﴿And He is the One﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿who multiplied you﴾, that is, created you and spread you ﴿throughout the earth﴾. And when He had reminded them of their origination, which implies the power to restore them, together with the wisdom in it and the disruption of wisdom in neglecting it, He stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿And to Him﴾, that is, to Him alone, ﴿you will be gathered﴾ on the Day of Resurrection.

(p-174) When this (principle) had included their giving life and their causing death, he stated it explicitly in a general form, saying: ﴿And He﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿is the One who﴾ it is in His nature that ﴿gives life and causes death﴾, so nothing prevents Him from resurrection, nor from anything else He wills. And since the true reality of resurrection is the bringing into existence of a thing as it is after its annihilation, He reminded them of a matter with which they had long been familiar, dealt with, and practiced, saying: ﴿And His is﴾, that is, His alone and not another's, ﴿the alternation of the night and the day﴾, that is, the disposing of both in this manner, each one brought into being after He has annihilated it, just as it was, identically. Their succession indicates their change, and their change through this, and through increase and decrease, indicates that they have a Changer who does not change, and that they have no action of their own; rather, the action belongs to Him alone. And (it indicates) that He is capable of restoring what has ceased to exist, just as He was capable of originating it, by means of that which points to His power, and by this evident proof (dalil shuhudi) for those who reflect. Therefore He concluded it with His words, rebuking them for the lack of their reasoning: ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾, that is, will you not have intellects with which you would come to know this, and then act upon what it requires of belief in the resurrection, which necessitates following the (straight) path (al-sirat).

Since the meaning of the rhetorical interrogation (al-istifham al-inkari) is negation, the words that follow it, "Bal" (rather), are most fitting in the fullest sense. He shifted to the third-person form of address (uslub al-ghayba) to signal anger with His saying: ﴿They said﴾, that is, these Arabs ﴿the same as what the ancients said﴾ from the people of Noah and those after him.

Then he resumed his speech: ﴿They said﴾, that is, denying the resurrection and marveling (مُتَعَجِّبِينَ) at his matter: ﴿When we die and become dust and bones?﴾ That is, we will be turned to dust after death, and bones (نَخِرَةً), decayed. Then they emphasized the denial with their words: ﴿Shall we indeed be raised up again?﴾ That is, from any raiser whatsoever.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 83:

Since the focus of concern in this surah is creation and bringing into existence, and the warning is directed at the people of obstinacy, He relates of them that they said: ﴿Indeed we have been promised﴾, placing their saying ﴿we and our fathers﴾ before their saying ﴿this﴾, that is, the resurrection, ﴿from before﴾. This is in contrast to Surah al-Naml, for the focus of concern there is faith in the Hereafter, and therefore it placed his saying "this" first. The intended meaning is the promise made to their fathers through the tongues of the messengers who came to them, except that the report that it encompasses them made it a promise to all alike. Then they resumed their saying: ﴿This is not﴾, that is, ﴿nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾, that is, a lie with no reality to it, because that is the meaning of emphatic denial.

Now when they denied the Resurrection with this emphatic denial, and rejected it with this definite rejection, He commanded him to confront them with matters they acknowledge and know well, from whose acceptance the affirmation of the Resurrection necessarily follows with certainty. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, responding to their denial of the Resurrection and binding them to it: ﴿To whom belongs the earth﴾, that is, with its vastness and the abundance of its wonders, ﴿and whoever is in it﴾, with their multitude and diversity, ﴿if you know﴾, that is, with knowledge that is, as it were, innate to you. And this is an alert to them that they denied something that no sane person would deny.

Since they acknowledged that, he reported their answer before they gave it, so that it would be among the proofs of prophethood and signs of the message, saying in a resumed statement: ﴿They will say﴾, that is, certainly: all of that is ﴿for God﴾, that is, the One specially characterized by the attributes of perfection. Since that indicates His oneness and His singularity in complete power in two respects, namely that all of that belongs to Him and that He reports about His enemy something which He cannot fail to bring about, He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them, when they say that to you, rebuking them for their failure to take heed, even to the least degree, by what the idgham (assimilation) indicates: ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾, that is, by that which is settled in your natures and which you hold as certain, of the complete power of Him and the dazzling greatness of which you have been heedless, so that you would believe what He reported of the resurrection, which is less than that, and know that none of these things—which are His dominion—is fit to be a partner to Him (p-177) nor a son, and know that it is not at all consistent with wisdom that He would abandon the resurrection, because the least of you would not accept abandoning the reckoning of his servants and dealing justly between them.

When He had reminded them of the lower world because of its nearness, He followed it with the higher world because it is greater, saying, in that same pattern, leading them upward to it: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord﴾, that is, the Creator and Manager, ﴿of the seven heavens﴾ as you witness from their motions and the movement of their stars, ﴿and the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾, which you yourselves acknowledge.

Verse 87: ﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ That is, the One to whom belongs everything is the Lord of that. According to the reading of the Basrans, and the estimation in the other readings: all of that belongs to Allah, because the meaning of "who is the lord of a thing" (man rabbu al-shay') is "to whom does the thing belong," so the lam (ل) explicitly indicates ownership, along with the Lord (al-Rabb) indicating management (al-tadbir).

When the matter became firmly established and the clarity increased, the threat against persisting in it was fitting, so He said: ﴿Say﴾, rebuking them for not making fear of God (taqwa) a means for them: ﴿Will you not then be mindful of God?﴾ That is, do you not place between yourselves and the descent of wrath, from this One of vast dominion and complete power, a protection through repentance (al-mataab) from denying something that is trivial in comparison to this Great King, and easy for Him?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 23, verse 88:

When He had established with them the two worlds, the higher and the lower, He commanded him to establish with them what is more general than these two and greater, so He said: ﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion (malakut) of all things?"﴾ That is, specifically, ﴿the dominion of all things﴾, that is, of the two worlds and of other than them. Malakut is the perfect dominion (al-mulk al-baligh) in which there is no deficiency in any respect. Ibn Kathir said: When the Arabs had a chieftain among them, and he granted protection (ijarah) to anyone, no one would violate his protection, and no one below him could grant protection against him, lest he usurp his authority. Even if he granted protection, it would be of no benefit. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and He protects, and none can be protected against Him﴾. That is, He prevents and gives refuge to whomever He wills, so that he is in His safeguard, and no one can approach His court. ﴿And none can be protected against Him﴾, that is, no one is able, ever, to grant a protection that would stand above Him, by being contrary to His will. Rather, He seizes whom He wills, even if all creatures support him, and He exalts whom He wills, even if all calamities assail him. Thus it becomes clear, as plain as the sun, that He has no partner who could contend with Him, and no son who could be His counterpart or equal. Ibn Kathir said: He is the Supreme Lord, greater than whom there is none, to whom belong the creation and the command. None can reverse His judgment; He cannot be resisted or opposed. What He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be.

Since this is a proof, although it is evident and hidden from no one, one who has a purpose in obstinacy may hesitate about it. So He spurred them on to hasten to acknowledge it and stirred them with His words: ﴿if you know﴾, that is, with firm knowledge (kawnan rasikhan), ﴿you know﴾, that is, as among those who know.

ولِذَلِكَ اسْتَأْنَفَ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ أيِ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ذَلِكَ، خاصًّا بِهِ، والتَّقْدِيرُ لِغَيْرِ البَصْرِيِّينَ: ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ، (p-١٧٩)لِأنَّ اليَدَ أدَلُّ شَيْءٍ عَلى المِلْكِ.

For this reason he resumed (istinaf, beginning a new sentence) with His words: ﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ That is, to the One in whose hand is that, exclusively to Him. The estimated reading, according to those other than the al-Basriyyin (the grammarians of Basra), is: all of that belongs to Allah, because the hand is the strongest indication of ownership.

ولَمّا كانَ جَوابُهم بِذَلِكَ يَقْتَضِي إنْكارَ تَوَقُّفِهِمْ في الإقْرارِ بِالبَعْثِ، اسْتَأْنَفَ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿قُلْ﴾ مُنْكِرًا عَلَيْهِمْ تَسْبِيبَ ذَلِكَ لَهُمُ ادِّعاءَ أنَّهُ سِحْرٌ، أوِ الصَّرْفَ عَنِ الحَقِّ كَما يُصْرَفُ المَسْحُورُ ﴿فَأنّى تُسْحَرُونَ﴾ أيْ فَكَيْفَ بَعْدَ إقْرارِكم بِهَذا كُلِّهِ تَدَّعُونَ أنَّ الوَعِيدَ بِالبَعْثِ سِحْرٌ في قَوْلِكُمْ: أفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وأنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ، ومِن أيْنَ صارَ لَكم هَذا الِاعْتِقادُ وقَدْ أقْرَرْتُمْ بِما يَلْزَمُ مِنهُ شُمُولُ العِلْمِ وتَمامَ القُدْرَةِ؟ ومِن أيْنَ تَتَخَيَّلُونَ الحَقَّ باطِلًا، أوْ كَيْفَ تَفْعَلُونَ فِعْلَ المَسْحُورِ بِما تَأْتُونَ بِهِ مِنَ التَّخْطِيطِ في الأقْوالِ والأفْعالِ، وتُخْدَعُونَ وتُصْرَفُونَ عَنْ كُلِّ ما دَعا إلَيْهِ؟

Since their answer to that implies a denial of their hesitation in acknowledging the Resurrection, he resumed with His words: ﴿Say﴾, disapproving of them for attributing this to a cause, namely their claim that it is sorcery, or that they are turned away from the truth as one who is bewitched is turned away: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ That is: how, after your acknowledgment of all of this, do you claim that the threat of Resurrection is sorcery, in your saying: ﴿Will you approach magic while you see?﴾ And from where has this belief come to you, when you have acknowledged what necessarily entails the comprehensiveness of knowledge and the perfection of power? And from where do you imagine the truth to be falsehood? Or how do you act like one who is bewitched, by what you bring of scheming in words and deeds, and you are deceived and turned away from everything to which He has called?

When denial carries the sense of negation, his saying "Bal" (Nay/Rather) is apt, meaning: the matter is not as they claim. "We did not bring them magic, rather—" or the meaning may be: it is not myths, but rather ﴿We brought them﴾ therein, in Our greatness, ﴿with the truth﴾, that is the complete truth after which there is no truth, as the definite article (al) indicates. So everything He informed of, of tawhid (divine oneness), resurrection and other matters, is true. ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾ in their saying that it is sorcery with no reality, and in all that they claimed of offspring and partners and other things, whose falsehood the Qur'an has made clear, (p-180) just as they were held to account by what they themselves acknowledged in answer to these three questions.

When the greatest of their lies is what His saying the Exalted alludes to, ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son"﴾ (Al-Anbiya', 21:26), He said: ﴿Allah has not taken any son﴾, meaning the One who has no equal (kufu'). He stressed the negation with His words ﴿any son﴾, so that it excludes the angels and everyone else, since the proofs of His self-sufficiency and that He has no like had already been established. And since they had acknowledged that He grants protection and is not Himself protected against, and that to Him belong the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, the argument is binding upon them.

Since a son is more specific than a partner in general, He said: ﴿Nor was there with Him﴾, meaning in any way whatsoever, ﴿any god﴾. By the verb "was" He conveyed the negation of its validity, so that its existence is negated all the more. He added "any" (min) to reinforce the negation. And since their claim that divinity belongs to one with a son or with something else entailed falsehood, given their own acknowledgment, He established against it a rational proof, so that the binding argument (al-ilzami) and the rational argument (al-'aqli) would correspond. So He said: ﴿Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created﴾, meaning by disposing of it alone, so that what belongs to him would be distinguished from what belongs to others, ﴿and some of them would have overcome others﴾, meaning some of the gods over others, when their commands conflicted. Then none of them would be content for what he created to be attributed to another, nor for a matter to proceed in a way other than what he wills, as is the usual course of affairs. The one who is overcome would not be a god, because of his inability, and he would not be one who grants protection without being protected against. ﴿In His hand alone is the dominion of everything﴾. In this there is an indication that, had there been no such conflict, it would have been possible for it to occur, and the mere possibility of it suffices to refute partnership, because the possibility of inability follows from it, and inability contradicts divinity, as He explained in Al-Anbiya'.

Since the proof corresponded to the binding argument against any partner, He declared His own exalted Self free of what is the result of that, saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾, meaning the One characterized by all attributes of perfection, exalted above every trace of deficiency, ﴿above what they describe﴾, meaning every description unbefitting His sacred presence, such as partners, sons, and anything else.

Then he established another proof of His perfection by describing Him with His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾. And since knowledge of that does not necessarily entail knowledge of the witnessed (ash-shahadah), as in the case of one who is asleep, He said: ﴿and the witnessed﴾, and no one knows that other than Him.

And since it is clear and manifest that no one claims that, and whoever claims it other than Him, his lie becomes evident without doubt, and whoever's knowledge is complete, his power is complete, his uniqueness became clear, as He explained in Ta-Ha, His saying resulted from this: ﴿Exalted be He﴾, i.e., the Knower indicated was exalted with a great exaltation, ﴿above what they associate with Him﴾, for there is no knowledge of any of it, so there is no power, nor (p-182) suitability for the rank of divinity.

When he had established the proof of their lying through evidence of His greatness and His exaltedness above everything the wrongdoers say, and had made the matter perfectly clear to them, after having warned them with his saying "and they are unaware," and with ﴿until, when We seize their affluent ones with punishment﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 64], and similar things, and with what He sent down upon those who came before and what He brought down upon the deniers, it was known that after giving warning there is nothing but the carrying out of the decree and the sending down of affliction. It was also possible that He, glorified is He, would encompass the wrongdoer and others with His punishment, since He is not questioned about what He does. So He commanded him to seek refuge from that, to manifest the greatness of Lordship (al-rubūbiyyah) and the humility of servitude (al-'ubūdiyyah), and so He said, ﴿Say: My Lord﴾, meaning, O You who are good to me. He emphasized it to manifest the greatness of the One being called upon, and to make known the excess of compassion the Prophet (ﷺ) had for his community, both believing and disbelieving. ﴿If You show me﴾, meaning, if it must be that You show me before my death, ﴿what they are promised﴾.

Then He alerted him to increasing his supplication by repeating the call with the attribute of beneficence (ihsan), in worship and humility, and in abasement and submission, indicating that Allah, glory be to Him, may do whatever He wills, so it is fitting for the closest of His creation to Him to be in utmost caution before Him. So He said: ﴿My Lord, do not make me⁠﴾ among, by Your beneficence toward me and Your grace upon me regarding them. This was the original form, but He made the attribute apparent to generalize the supplication and to tie the ruling to the attribute, so He said: ﴿among the wrongdoing people⁠﴾, that is, those whose deeds are the deeds of one who walks in darkness, so they are misplaced, let alone that I should be among them, for the punishment is about to befall them specifically and to encompass those who live near them, because of the grave nature of wrongdoing and its evil consequence. (p-183)

Now that the particle of doubt has pointed to the sense that the intended meaning is: "Indeed We are able both to pardon them and to give them respite," he follows it with a statement that stresses what they have of denial, which implies a disparagement of [Divine] power, and they are the ones addressed by the threat: ﴿And indeed﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿We are able to show you﴾, that is, before your death, ﴿what We promise them﴾ of punishment, ﴿[indeed] able﴾.

When it became clear from this that their seizure and their respite were equally within God's power, and that they were saying and doing what cannot be endured except with help from God, it was as though He had said: "What should I do regarding what You know of their affair?" So He said, commanding him to treat it: ﴿Repel﴾, and He magnified the command by using the relative pronoun, because of the suggestive ambiguity in it that makes one eager for explanation; then by the superlative form, so He said: ﴿with that which is best﴾, meaning, of the words and deeds, by forgiveness and forbearance, ﴿the evil﴾. Then He lightened for him what he finds of its burden by His saying: ﴿We are most knowing﴾, meaning, more than any knower, ﴿of what they describe﴾ concerning your right and Our right. So if We willed, We would prevent them from it, or hasten punishment upon them; and no one is more jealous than Us. So be patient, as the steadfast ones among the messengers (ulu al-'azm) were patient.

Since patience in the face of this cannot be sustained except by Him, glory be to Him, He commanded him to supplicate for that, saying: ﴿And say: "My Lord"﴾ O You who bestow kindness upon me, ﴿I seek refuge in You﴾, that is, I take refuge with You (p-184) ﴿from the incitements of the devils﴾, that is, that they reach me with their whisperings, which are like the goad of the prod (mihmaz) in pushing toward misdeeds and distancing from all good deeds, so how much more from the better of them, just as You have set them upon the disbelievers, urging them toward vileness with a vigorous urging.

"And I seek refuge in You, my Lord" — that is, O You who nurture me — "from their being present with me" — that is, even if their whisperings do not reach me, for their presence is ruin, and their distance is blessing, because they are made by nature to corruption and never part from it.

When the most harmful of the times of their presence is the hour of death and the state of being overtaken, since it is the time when the veil is lifted from what was decreed by fate, the meeting draws near, and descent or ascent becomes inevitable, He followed that with mention of it, as an alert to exerting effort in supplication and humble entreaty for protection (*'ismah*) at that time. He said, linking it to His words ﴿but they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 56], or to *mublisun* (despairing), alerting by means of the particle of limit (*hatta*, "until") that He, glorified is He, prolongs their lifetimes as *istidraj* (gradual enticement, by which Allah leads the disbelievers on step by step). ﴿Until﴾, or the supposed construction, as the context indicates, is: "I shall not be among the disbelievers who obey the devils, until ﴿when death comes to one of them﴾." He placed the object before the subject so that the mind would wander in every direction regarding its doer, and then said ﴿death comes to one of them﴾. So He lifts the veil for him, the truth becomes manifest to him, and the flashes of punishment appear to him, and no doubt remains in any of that. ﴿He says﴾, addressing the angels of punishment, according to the habit of his ignorance and his fixation on the perceptible, (p-185) like the manner of beasts: ﴿My Lord, send me back﴾, that is, to the world, the abode of action. It is also permissible that the plural refers to God, exalted is He, and to the angels, or that it is a form of honoring, following the custom in addressing the great, especially kings, or for the purpose of repeating the verb for emphasis.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 100:

When he was in that state, certain of despair of salvation and therefore despairing of doing any good deed, since the abode of action had passed, and having reached the point of the death-rattle (al-gharghara), he said: ﴿My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind﴾, meaning: so that I may be in hope of doing righteous deeds ﴿in what I have left behind﴾ of faith and its consequences. Al-Baghawi said: Qatada said: He did not wish to return to his family and his clan, nor to gather worldly wealth and fulfil his desires; rather he wished to return in order to act in obedience to Allah. May Allah have mercy on a man who acts in what the disbeliever wishes for when he sees the punishment.

Ibn Kathir said: Al-Ala' ibn Ziyad used to say: Let each of you imagine himself as one whom death has come to, so that he asks his Lord for a reprieve and He grants it to him, and then let him act in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic.

Since the decree had definitively settled that he would not return, and even if he were returned he would not act, He said, as a rebuke to him and a rejection of his words: ﴿No!﴾, meaning: none of that will happen. It is as if it was said: What is the ruling on what he said? So He said, turning away from him as a sign of anger: ﴿Indeed, it is a word﴾, meaning his statement ﴿My Lord, send me back﴾ to the end of the verse, a word ﴿he is saying﴾, and it is known from his deceit and lying, so it is, as is his habit, without any reality.

Since the implied sense is: he will not be answered in it, He joined to it His saying, bringing together with him everyone like him, because the incapacity of the group entails the incapacity of the individual: ﴿And before them is a barrier﴾, meaning behind them and in front of them, encompassing them, ﴿a barrier﴾, meaning a partition between where they are and the world and the Resurrection, lasting, which no one can remove, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, meaning their resurrection is renewed by the easiest, lightest and least difficult matter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 101:

And when that was limited by the Resurrection (al-Ba'th), the soul longed for what would come after it. It had already been stated that people, after having been one community in gathering before their Lord, had split into pieces, formed themselves into factions, and by virtue of that supported and aided one another. Negating that, He said: ﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown﴾, that is, with the easiest of matters, the second blast, which is the blast of rising (nushur), or the third, which is for the swoon (sa'q), ﴿on the Trumpet﴾, so they rise from the graves (p-187) or from the swoon. ﴿There will be no kinship (ansab)﴾, and it is the greatest of the means, ﴿between them﴾, which they would mention, boasting by it, ﴿that Day﴾, because of the matter that overwhelms them, the distress that occupies them, the bewilderment that reaches them, and the terror that frightens them from the dread, and because they know that it benefits nothing except what God permits. Rather, a person flees from the nearest of people to him. Their kinship is only their righteous deeds. ﴿And they will not ask of one another﴾, that is, in seeking help, because it has become clear to them that there is no judgment except God's, and that no soul avails another soul anything. Consequently it follows that there is no support except through deeds, God having shown mercy by facilitating them, then having shown mercy by accepting them. Therefore He said.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 102:

﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy﴾ i.e., with accepted deeds. Perhaps the plural (mawazin, "scales") is used because each deed has its own scale, which knows that no other is suitable for it, and this is more indicative of [God's] power. ﴿Then those﴾ i.e., specifically, perhaps he used the plural for the glad tidings of the great number of the saved, after having used the singular to indicate the abundance of deeds, or to indicate that the weighing applies to every individual. ﴿They are the successful﴾ because they are the believers who are described [by these attributes].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 103:

﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾ because of his turning away from those deeds founded upon faith, ﴿those are they﴾ specifically ﴿who have lost their souls﴾ by destroying them through following their desires in the abode of deeds and by preoccupying themselves with their whims away from the ranks of perfection. Then he explained or gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿in Hell will they abide forever﴾, and it is an abode whose captive is never released and whose blaze is never extinguished.

Then he resumed his statement: ﴿Talfah﴾ (it scorches, i.e., it covers) with its intense heat, its scorching blast and its blaze ﴿their faces, the Fire﴾, so it burns them, and so how much more will it burn others. ﴿And they therein are grimacing﴾, i.e., their lips are drawn back from their teeth, with the faces frowning, wrinkled and contorted, the condition of one whose inner self is filled with aversion to what has overwhelmed him of intense suffering and great affliction in the abode of grimness, just as you see severely roasted heads. The negation of questioning here does not contradict its affirmation elsewhere, because that is in a different situation: not in mutual aid, but in mutual blame, reproach and enmity. Moreover, the standing-places on that Day are long and many, so the statements and conditions differ and multiply accordingly. And there will come from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, something similar to this in Surat al-Saffat.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 105:

When it is the customary way that the one punished by deed is also joined with speech, he is answered, regarding one who may ask about that, by His saying: ﴿Did not﴾, that is, it is said to them in rebuke and reproach: Did not ﴿My verses come to you﴾, whose greatness reached the highest ranks by their being attributed to Me. And since the mere mention of them was sufficient for faith, He drew attention to this by the passive construction: ﴿They were recited to you﴾, that is, their recitation was continued for you in the world little by little. And since they were a cause of faith, and you made them a cause of disbelief, He said: ﴿so you used to deny them﴾, that is, in a state in which you were deeply immersed, ﴿with them﴾. And he placed the adverbial phrase first (p-189) to inform that they exaggerated in denial.

Then he resumed their reply with his words: ﴿They say, "Our Lord,"﴾ O You who bestow Your blessings upon us, ﴿our wretchedness overcame us﴾, that is, our desires, which led us to evil deeds, which were the apparent cause of wretchedness.

And since the implied sense is: "So we were with them like captives, whom the devils drove toward them with a driving," he followed it with his words ﴿and we were﴾, that is, by what He had created us upon, ﴿a people astray﴾ in that, far from guidance, strong in the requirements of wretchedness, and so it was a cause of straying from the path of happiness.

"Since this acknowledgment contained an apology, and that might have been a ground for deliverance, they joined to it their saying: ﴿Our Lord﴾, O You who have accustomed us to goodness, ﴿bring us out of it﴾, that is, out of the Fire, by Your bounty, following the custom of Your generosity, and return us to the abode of the world so that we may do what pleases You. ﴿But if we return﴾ to the like of those errors, ﴿then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾. So their answer was resumed with ﴿inna﴾ (indeed, verily)."

Allah said: "Remain silent in it (the Fire) and do not speak to Me." Just as one says to a dog, "Be gone!" — that is, drive yourselves off like a dog is driven off, and be cast away from addressing Me, silent in the silence of humiliation. "In it" — that is, in the Fire. "And do not speak to Me" at all, for you are not worthy of being addressed by Me, because you have never ceased to be characterized by wrongdoing. Among this is your present request, which implies that your being characterized by it is only conceivable on the supposition that you would return after being brought out.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 23, verse 109:

When mockery is the most delightful joy for the mocker and the most humiliating disgrace for the one mocked, he gave the reason for that by his saying: ﴿Indeed, there was\] a group﴾ — that is, a firmly established state — ﴿a group﴾, that is, people whom you made weak, so that their separation from you was easy for you, and your separation from them, and you thought that you would scatter their gathering, ﴿of My servants﴾, that is, those who are fit to be ascribed to My presence, because of their sincerity, free from desires, ﴿who say﴾ continually: ﴿"Our Lord"﴾, O You who bestow kindness upon us by creation and provision, ﴿"we have believed"﴾, that is, we have brought about belief in all that the Messengers brought to us, because that is obligatory upon us by Your command to us regarding it.

When the greatness of the station necessitates the shortcoming of the worshipper, and acknowledging the shortcoming is a remedy for it, they said: ﴿"So forgive us"﴾, that is, cover over, by means of our belief, our faults through which our shortcoming was caused, ﴿"and have mercy upon us"﴾, that is, deal with us in the manner of one who is merciful, with the good that is in the form of tenderness, compassion and kindness.

When the implied meaning is: "Then You are the best of those who forgive," for when You cover a sin You cause it to be forgotten by everyone, even by the recording angels, He followed it with His saying: ﴿"And You are the best of the merciful"﴾, because You deliver whomever You have mercy upon from every wretchedness and humiliation, through the sincerity of faith and deliverance from every disbelief.

(p-191) When the increase in disbelief of those others was caused by the faith of these people, He said: ﴿So you took them in derision﴾, i.e., as objects of mockery, amusement, and service to you. Al-Shihab al-Samin said in his i'rab (grammatical analysis): "As-suhrah (with a dammah) means being made to serve; suhriyyan (with a dammah, from it) and as-suhr (without the ha') mean mockery. The form with kasrah from it, according to both readings, indicates an increase in the intensity of the action, as in khusූsiyyah (particularity) and ubudiyyah (servitude)." ﴿Until they made you forget﴾, i.e., because they were the cause of that through your preoccupation with ridiculing them and considering them far-fetched, ﴿My remembrance﴾, i.e., that you should remember Me and thereby fear Me, by your fully devoting yourselves to that against them.

Since the implied sense was: "So you abandoned Him and did not guard your duty to Me regarding My friends," He followed it with His words: ﴿And you used to laugh﴾, i.e., by characteristics that were like innate nature, ﴿at them﴾, i.e., specifically, ﴿laughing﴾. As though, when they directed their faculties toward mocking them, they counted others' laughter as nothing.

When the soul had longed, after learning what was done to their enemies, to know their recompense, He said: ﴿Indeed I have rewarded them today for what they endured﴾, that is, as a repayment for their deeds, ﴿for what they endured﴾, that is, for their worship of Me; their suffering at your hands did not distract them from it as your delight in humiliating them distracted you from it. Their triumph is theirs alone, apart from you. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿that they are they﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿the victorious﴾, that is, (p-192) the saved, the triumphant who attain good after having been on the brink of destruction. He changed the expression to convey exclusivity, clarity and firmness. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read the hamzah with a kasra, treating it as a fresh (resumptive) sentence (isti'naf).

When the successful one, meaning the victorious one, is he who is not afflicted with misery in that matter in which he triumphed, and He (glory be to Him) had already indicated, through the particle of limit (*harf al-ghayah*, the particle denoting an end point) and what resembles it, that He extended to the people of wretchedness in the world in their lifespans and provisions until they came to disdain the worship of the happy ones, it might be said that their enemies had triumphed by mocking them and rising above them in the life of this world. He (glory be to Him) had already forestalled this by informing that He made them abide in the Fire, turned away from them, and rebuked them for speaking to Him. The most comfortable of the people of the world, when he is dipped once into the Fire and then asked about his comfort, says: "I have never seen comfort at all." This was a sharp reproach to the wretched for having wasted their days and for their regret over them. The listener yearns to know whether He will ask them about the blessings He bestowed upon them in the world, which deserved their gratitude, and which they met with disbelief and mockery of His friends. He answered this yearning by making them ignorant, rebuking them, and alerting to the answer, that their triumph in the world, given its brevity, which is more insignificant than a drop beside an ocean, is non-existent. This is in His saying: ﴿He said﴾, expressing regret over what they neglected of a small worship that would have yielded an endless happiness, and what they committed of a brief pleasure that brought them a misery without end. This is according to the reading of the majority (*al-jama'ah*). Glory be to Him, by the reading of Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i (*qira'at* meaning canonical recitations), clarified that the speech comes through some of His servants whom He appointed to punish them, as a turning away from them, confirming what He had indicated in His saying ﴿and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, O you whom We have appointed for vengeance against whomever We wish, namely these people whom the life of this world deceived, in view of its brief duration as they see it and its play with its people, so they disbelieved in Us and mocked Our servants: ﴿How many years did you remain on the earth?﴾ in that state which you used to consider a triumph, ﴿the number of years﴾ in which you were victorious and your enemies were subdued. Perhaps He expressed it by what carries the sense of *al-isnat* (drought, scarcity), whose meaning is famine, to indicate that the days of the world are narrow and distressing, even if they contain some abundance, and especially for the disbelievers, because of their disbelief, their corruption and their scheming, which drew them into the most constricted narrowness and the worst of living.

They said, belittling it in comparison with the torment they had witnessed, and seeking to save themselves, supposing that the length of their stay in the Fire would be equal to their stay in the world: ﴿We remained a day﴾. Perhaps they mentioned the operative verb out of delight in prolonging the speech, or to state the intended meaning explicitly, averting confusion and doubt. Then they increased the minimization and said: ﴿or part of a day﴾.
